prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” HVAC company for every homeowner — the right choice depends on your budget, the size/age of your home, timing, brand preference, warranty needs, and whether you want high-efficiency equipment or just a reliable replacement. I can help you pick one, but first a few quick questions:

- Is this for a single-family home or a business?  
- What city/ZIP or neighborhood in Atlanta? (helps me find local contractors near you)  
- Do you know the system size (tons) or square footage of the home?  
- Any brand preference (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Rheem, Goodman, etc.) or desire for high-efficiency (16–20+ SEER)?  
- Target budget or need for financing?

If you want immediate guidance, here’s a short checklist and process to find the best local contractor:

1. What to require from any contractor
   - Current license and proof of insurance (liability and workers’ comp).  
   - NATE-certified technicians or equivalent training.  
   - Written estimate with line items: equipment, labor, permit fees, removal of old unit, and final testing/balancing.  
   - Agreement to perform a Manual J load calculation and sizing (not just “replace like-for-like”).  
   - Clear warranty details: manufacturer warranty and contractor/installation warranty.  
   - Permits and code-compliant work (contractor should pull permits).

2. How to compare bids
   - Get at least 3 written quotes.  
   - Compare total installed cost, equipment model/SEER, estimated seasonal energy usage, and warranty length.  
   - Beware very low bids — they often cut corners or use inferior parts.  
   - Ask about the refrigerant type (R-410A common now), estimated start-to-finish timeline, and any needed ductwork or airflow fixes.

3. Red flags
   - Pressure to sign immediately or cash-only deals.  
   - No physical address or poor online reviews.  
   - Refusal to pull permits or do a load calculation.  
   - Vague warranty language (make sure it’s written).

4. Sources to vet companies
   - Google/Google Maps reviews, Yelp (read recent reviews).  
   - Better Business Bureau for complaints and responses.  
   - Local utility rebates (Georgia Power, etc.) — some contractors help you claim rebates.  
   - Ask neighbors/homeowners’ association for recommendations.

5. Typical costs & efficiency notes (ballpark)
   - Full central AC replacement commonly ranges widely (roughly $3,500–$12,000) depending on equipment, home size, and ductwork.  
   - Upgrading SEER improves efficiency but costs more upfront. A 14–16 SEER unit is common; 18–20+ SEER is high-efficiency.

If you want, I can:
- Look up well-reviewed HVAC contractors in your part of Atlanta (tell me your ZIP) and give you a short list with pros/cons, or  
- Draft an email or script you can use to request quotes and ask the right questions.

Which would you like to do?
